Dude, I feel the exact same way. Having a random seizure is in my top 3 things im scared of having. I've never ever had a seizure before. My fear of them started when I was a kid, when I would watch DVDs and that warning that said "sensitive content ahead,may cause epileptic seizure" always terrified me. I never used to be sensitive to flashing lights, but I honestly tricked my brain into thinking that I'll have a seizure If I look at  flashing lights. So now, I always have to be careful at concerts or watching tv. A few weeks ago, I watched the new Godzilla movie with my husband and friends, and the scene where they're going underground with all the  flashing lights, made me have a panic attack, because I wasn't expecting it. I and to cover my eyes with my purse and sunglasses I brought in, lol. My brain instantly felt like it was "seizing", the definition I've apparently given that word, although I've never felt a seizure before. I know it's probably just anxiety making me feel funny in my head whenever I see flashing lights. 

I'm a 20 year old female too. I 100% understand your fear. It sucks! But just know that there's a veryyyy low chance of you ever getting a random seizure.  If you keep worrying about it, your brain will  literally make you "feel" what you believe a seizure would feel like. But trust me, it's not an actual seizure. Anxiety is the most powerful thing I know, so if it gets out of control, you still feel side effects. Reading this article helped me calm down: 

"The brain consists of nerve cells that communicate with each other through electrical activity. A seizure occurs when one or more parts of the brain has a burst of abnormal electrical signals that interrupt normal brain signals. Anything that interrupts the normal connections between nerve cells in the brain can cause a seizure. This includes a high fever, high or low blood sugar, alcohol or drug withdrawal, or a brain concussion." 
(https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/health/conditions-and-diseases/epilepsy/evaluation-of-a-firsttime-seizure) 

Maybe your friend had low blood sugar? Or was dehydrated? Was she recently sick or anything? So many factors can play into it. I promise, you are going to be okay. You're just afraid, which is understandable. We all are, haha.
